model: HK416 D14.5RS barrel and handguard heating
frame: z_mm is the asset frame: +Z towards the muzzle, 0 at the upper receiver front face (barrel breech at -5 mm)

charge_mass_g.source: action.json m_charge: M855, 26.1 gr WC844 (US Army TM 43-0001-27)

propellant_energy_J_per_g.source: action.json: F / (gamma - 1), the energy the gas can give up (force 1.0 MJ/kg, gamma 1.24)

bore_heat_scale.source: multiplier on the Dittus-Boelter bore heat-transfer coefficient. 1.0 = the correlation as published, NOT fitted; the fire-to-destruction counts check it

f_chamber.source: CALIBRATED on the NSWC Crane M4A1 chamber temperatures (first firing sequence): heat per unit length into the chamber wall relative to the first bore station; see README

g_chamber_case.source: inferred: contact conductance between the chamber wall and the chambered round, 1000 W/m2/K over the 1100 mm2 case wall of action.json. The Crane data support it weakly: see validation.fit_scan

c_case_J_K.source: heat capacity of the brass case: action.json m_case 6.2 g x 380 J/kg/K (C26000 handbook)

case_wall_m.source: inferred: mean 5.56 mm case wall over the body and shoulder (0.3 mm at the neck to about 1 mm near the head)

chamber_h_ratio.source: inferred: gas-side heat-transfer coefficient inside the case relative to the first bore station (half the gas speed, to the power 0.8)

friction_to_bore.source: inferred: share of the bullet friction and engraving work (action.json p_friction, p_engrave) that stays in the bore; the rest leaves in the jacket

q_port_J.source: inferred: extra bore heating around the gas port (Purdue thesis: port heating "should not be neglected")

piston_share.source: inferred: share of the gas-cylinder wall heat taken by the piston and rod, the rest by the gas block

q_gas_block_di_J.source: inferred, validation rifles only: a direct-impingement gas block keeps little heat (the gas goes down the tube)

q_flash_hider_J.source: inferred: muzzle gas washing the birdcage; large uncertainty

hg_area_m2.source: metal cross-section: 0.20 m perimeter x 3 mm wall + four rails, less vents -> 0.40 kg (inferred from the build.py section)

hg_perim_out_m.source: convecting perimeter: 0.20 m envelope x 1.3 for rail lugs (inferred)

hg_view_to_ambient.source: fraction of barrel radiation leaving through vents and the open front (vent area / wall area, build.py)

hg_vent_fraction.source: inferred: share of the gap convection carried straight out of the vents and front

hg_top_bottom_split.source: inferred: top of the handguard runs this fraction of its excess hotter than the mean, the bottom half that cooler

g_barrel_nut.source: inferred: barrel flange clamped by the nut at 110 N m, 200 mm2 at 20 kW/m2/K

g_nut_handguard.source: inferred: sliding fit of the rail on the barrel nut, 2000 mm2 at 1.5 kW/m2/K

g_nut_upper.source: inferred: nut threads on the 7075 receiver ring

g_barrel_upper.source: inferred: barrel extension, slip fit in the receiver bore

m_nut.source: build.py barrel_nut: 29 mm OD, 19.8 mm ID, 22 mm long

g_upper_front_rear.source: inferred: 450 mm2 of receiver wall over 90 mm

g_handguard_upper.source: inferred: handguard rear face against the receiver

g_barrel_gas_block.source: inferred: pinned gas block journal, 1050 mm2 at 5 kW/m2/K

g_gas_block_piston.source: inferred: piston with three rings in the cylinder cup

g_barrel_fh.source: steel 160 mm2 over 15 mm between the threads and the birdcage (build.py)

m_gas_block.source: build.py gas block prism 72 g + front sight base 30 g (volume x 7850)

m_fh_front.source: build.py birdcage ahead of the muzzle, slots removed

m_upper_front.source: inferred: front 50 mm of the upper receiver

m_upper_rear.source: inferred: rest of the upper receiver

cyclic_rpm.source: action.json auto.rpm, the simulated cyclic rate (HK manual p. 7: 700 to 900)

k_steel.source: linear fit to ASM handbook 4140 (42.7 at 100 C, 33 at 600 C)

c_steel.source: Eurocode 3 part 1-2 specific heat of carbon steel, incl. the 735 C transformation peak; 440 at 20 C

c_al.source: handbook 6061 (896 at 25 C, about 1020 at 300 C)

shot_heat.method: Dittus-Boelter Nu = 0.023 Re^0.8 Pr^0.4 on the gas state of ../action/action.json (pressure, gas temperature, bullet travel and speed, Lagrange velocity profile), 1D conduction into the wall; blowdown continued to 1.05 atm
shot_heat.action_json_loss_factor_note: action.json assumes heat loss while the bullet is in the bore = loss_factor x work on bullet and gas; compare bore_J.while_bullet_in_bore

fit_scan.note: the alternative without round cooling, f_chamber refitted

marsh_first_sequence_error_C.note: 14 points x 2 barrel profiles; f_chamber was fitted to these

marsh_second_sequence_error_C.note: magazines 8 to 14 after the reload pause, 14 points x 2 barrel profiles, NOT used in the fit

destruction_published.colt_video: Colt test, M4 on automatic, magazines changed as fast as possible: barrel ruptured at 535 rounds after about two minutes (1 min 51 s in the earlier build's notes); heavy-barrel M4A1: 911 rounds, then the gas tube failed, barrel intact (New York Times At War blog, 12 Jan 2010, as summarised by AccurateShooter and others)
destruction_published.windham: J. Windham, Fire to Destruction Test of 5.56mm M4A1 Carbine and M16A2 Rifle Barrels, AMSTA-AR-ES-96-2, 1996 (DTIC ADA317929): M16A2 barrel ruptured at 491 rounds, M4A1 at 540 to 596 (figures from secondary accounts; the report itself could not be re-read for this build)
destruction_published.rupture_temperature: 817 C (1090 K) is the simulated rupture temperature of a Purdue thesis (AAI30501545, 548 rounds, 0.092 m from the breech); 737 C is quoted from a 1996 Army message as weak enough to burst. Both are secondary; the model reports when its hottest outer station passes each

rounds_to_180C_chamber.published: TM 9-1005-319-10: 140 rounds fired rapidly and continuously bring an M16A2 barrel to the cook-off point (150 for the M4 and 180 for the M4A1 in later editions, from the earlier build's notes); the TM gives neither the rate nor the temperature, so 90 rounds/min and 180 C are INFERRED

geometry.source: ../model/build.py build_barrel() and P; barrel extension radius and bore radii as noted in sim.py

semi_45.title: Semi-automatic, 45 rounds/min (manual: maximum effective rate, semi), 300 rounds

auto_bursts.title: Automatic, 5-round bursts at 800 rounds/min cyclic, 3 s between bursts, 5 s reloads, 210 rounds

auto_mag_dumps.title: Automatic, 30-round magazines emptied at 800 rounds/min cyclic, 5 s reloads, 210 rounds

manual_250_in_3min.title: HK manual's limit: 250 rounds in 3 minutes (83 rounds/min, evenly paced)

auto_to_destruction.title: Beyond the manual: 30-round magazines at cyclic, 4 s reloads, 600 rounds (where glow starts)

glow.note: grey body, emissivity 0.85; luminance from Planck x CIE 1931 y-bar (Wyman et al. 2013 fits); sRGB chromaticity normalised to max 1
glow.threshold_note: Draper point, 525 C (798 K): the classical limit of visible incandescence in darkness

mirage.note: two line plumes: above the exposed barrel and above the handguard top; values on the sight line 65.5 mm above the bore

formula.dT: min(2.6 F^(2/3) Ta / (g y), 0.5 dT_surface); cross-wind U > w: min(.., F Ta / (g U y))
formula.jitter_rad: 0.3 dn sqrt(2 sqrt(pi) L / b) exp(-(U / 0.35 w)^2)
formula.strength: dn at 30 mm above the hotter source / (0.0796 / Ta) = dT / (Ta + dT)

levels.name: comfortable
levels.note: below 43 C: ISO 13732-1 gives 43 C as the burn threshold for contact of 8 h and longer

levels.name: warm
levels.note: 43 to 48 C: can be held; ISO 13732-1 burn threshold for 10 min contact with uncoated metal is 48 C

levels.name: hot
levels.note: 48 to 51 C: ISO 13732-1 burn threshold for 1 min contact with uncoated metal is 51 C; MIL-STD-1472 limit for prolonged bare-hand contact with metal is 49 C

levels.name: burn_within_a_minute
levels.note: 51 to 60 C: ISO 13732-1 10 s threshold is about 55 C; MIL-STD-1472 momentary-contact limit for metal is 60 C

levels.name: burn_on_grip
levels.note: 60 to 70 C: burns within seconds; ISO 13732-1 burn threshold spread for 1 s contact with uncoated metal is 65 to 70 C

levels.name: burn_on_touch
levels.note: above 70 C: beyond the ISO 13732-1 1 s burn threshold for bare metal

skin.note: contact temperature of two half-spaces: (b_metal T_metal + b_skin T_skin) / (b_metal + b_skin), b = sqrt(k rho c); skin 33 C and b = 1300 W s^0.5/m2/K are INFERRED typical values

comfort.sources: ISO 13732-1:2006, burn thresholds for bare skin on uncoated metal: 1 s 65 to 70 C, 10 s about 55 C, 1 min 51 C, 10 min 48 C, 8 h 43 C; MIL-STD-1472 (metal: momentary contact 60 C, prolonged 49 C)
comfort.note: thresholds are for bare skin on bare metal (hard anodising is too thin to help); gloves or polymer rail covers raise them by tens of kelvin

cookoff.model: the brass case of the chambered round follows the chamber wall through g_chamber_case (time constant c_case/g = 2.4 s); the propellant on the case wall fires when the integral of dt / induction(T_case) reaches 1
anchors: 170 C, 600 s: smokeless (nitrocellulose) propellant self-ignites at about 160 to 200 C on slow heating (handbook range; INFERRED choice of point)
220 C, 10 s: TM 9-1005-319-10 warns that a round left in a barrel at the cook-off point may fire in as little as 10 seconds (INFERRED temperature)
checks: NSWC Crane (Marsh 2006, slide 8): rounds soaked in a 330 F (166 C) chamber for 15, 30 and 60 s were then fired for pressure; none is reported to have cooked off. Model: 874 s at 166 C
Marsh 2006, slide 2: M16-family chambers reach 400 F (204 C) in extreme use. Model at 204 C: 42 s

bow.method: INFERRED: top-to-bottom temperature difference across the barrel = eta x local excess temperature (the top of a hot horizontal cylinder sits in its own plume, and the gas block and piston are above the bore); curvature = alpha * eta * dT / D; muzzle angle = its integral over the free length ahead of the barrel nut; the muzzle points DOWN, so impact moves low
bow.source: mechanism: thermal bow of a beam with a linear temperature difference across it (Timoshenko, thermal stresses in beams; curvature = alpha dT / depth); the 1 % asymmetry is a guess, not a measurement

velocity.method: the propellant of the chambered round follows the case with a 25 s lag (INFERRED: conduction into a 9 mm bed of grains); muzzle velocity rises 0.85 m/s per K of propellant temperature above 25 C, up to 166 C
velocity.source: Marsh 2006 slide 8 pressures (65,172 psi after 15 s at 200 F; 85,662 psi after 60 s at 330 F, lot BLH03M032) with v ~ p^0.4 (INFERRED exponent)
velocity.use: pass 850 + mv_delta to HK416Ballistics.fire({muzzleVelocity}) to get the change of drop at any range

mirage.method: the optical shift of the target image through the plume is series mirage_steady_moa; it moves the picture, not the bullet

runtime.note: generated by sim.py; arrays are row-major [station][radial cell]; SI units, kelvin inside

skin.note: contact temperature of two half-spaces: (b_metal T_metal + b_skin T_skin) / (b_metal + b_skin), b = sqrt(k rho c); skin 33 C and b = 1300 W s^0.5/m2/K are INFERRED typical values

accuracy_vs_full_grid.note: runtime grid 74 x 3 at dt 0.0487 s against the full grid 146 x 4
